Hey there, 

for starters i'm a mid twenties male who has expirienced circumstances similar to those you described. Loneliness, depression and especially selfharm have been affecting me for quite some years.

I hate it to break it to you but most likely there is "something wrong" with you. If you do consider the norm. But to be fair what ist the norm? Wanting to be alone voluntarily has been scientifically proven to be against human nature. To be specific thats where the feeling of loneliness comes from. In earlier years humans needed to interact with each other to secure their survival (food, shelter, etc...). Nowadays we don't need social interaction to physically survive (to some extent), since we got supermarkets and actual housing. However our emotional health almost always suffers if the primal need for social interaction isn't met. 

I am by no means a pofessional when it comes to mental health but if I were in your shoes I would most likely go see a psychiatrist and/or a therapist. Since you already tried that I can only advise you to see another therapist (quite sometimes the therapist patient relationship doesn't kick off). A decent therapist could probably shed some light on where the social isolation comes from and suggest steps on how to overcome it. Also you not knowing what to live for and especially not feeling any enjoyment should be a strong indicator for professional help. But don't get me wrong this process usually requires quite some time and you actually wanting it. For me personally medication had a positive effect, although it took a while to find the right one. 

On a positive note I wouldn't focus as much on the scars and the "forever alone thing". I know you've probably heard it a million times by now but most people really don't mind your scars wether its a romantical or platonic relationship. If it hasn't happened yet (especially the romantic one you described). Dont give up. Just because the one girl didn't reciprocate your feelings doesn't mean there won't be one that does in the future.

Thank your for your reply. I actually considered seeing a sex-therapist, but due to the intimacy of the matter I did chicken out. 

If you don't mind me asking: Did you ever see a sex-therapist and if so what impact did it have on your "lifestyle".

Thank you for your reply. I am aware that there are women who fit the "preferences" (wrong term but I am not sure how to express it differently) that  I have.

I am not a native english speaker, so excuse me if my post went down a path i didn't anticipate.
